simple.meaning: בָּרַח (bârach) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “to bolt , i.e. figuratively, to flee suddenly.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 65 times across Genesis, Exodus, Numbers, Judges, 1 Samuel, and 15 more, beginning at Genesis 16:6. Its contexts include family, family line, mountain.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to בָּרַח (H1272).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: בָּרַח (bârach) / H1272 is traced through Genesis 16:6, Genesis 16:8, Genesis 27:43, Genesis 31:20 as a generated source-based concept entry.
